message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by taking home the lasagna from the potluck. Let me start by going through the situation step by step. First, I made lasagna and brought it over to my boyfriend's friend's potluck. When I got there, I noticed that the host had also made lasagna. The difference was that hers was already cooked, while mine needed to be reheated. She didn't bother to reheat mine, which I guess is why it was left untouched. She was also really rude when she saw that I brought lasagna, telling me that nobody could compete with hers, and she didn't want to put mine out to save me from embarrassment. Now, I'm a broke college student, and that lasagna could have lasted me a whole week. So, I decided to take it home. My friends also took home their untouched chips and pop, so I thought it was okay to do the same. But then the host got upset and texted me, saying I shouldn't have brought it home because they expected to have it for dinner tomorrow. She also said it's not nice to bring home leftovers. I've never been to a potluck before, so I didn't know the rules. My friend told me it was okay to take leftovers home, so I went ahead with that. Now I'm wondering if I did the right thing or not. Let me think about the possible reasons why she was upset. Maybe in potluck settings, people expect that all the food brought will be consumed there, and taking it home is considered rude. Or perhaps she felt that by taking my lasagna home, I was implying that hers wasn't good enough, which might have hurt her feelings. She was already rude about my lasagna, so maybe she was sensitive about her cooking. On the other hand, I was in a situation where I couldn't afford to waste food, especially something that could last me a week. My friends took their leftovers, so I thought it was acceptable. But maybe there's a difference between taking your own food versus someone else's. Or perhaps the host had a specific plan for the food, and taking it home disrupted that plan. I also need to consider the social norms around potlucks. From what I know, usually, people bring food to share, and it's expected that everyone will eat together. Taking food home might not be the norm, especially if the host has already provided enough. But I'm not sure if that's a universal rule or just specific to certain groups. Another angle is the emotional aspect. The host was already rude, so maybe she was upset because she felt disrespected when I took my lasagna home. She might have seen it as me not trusting her judgment or not valuing her efforts. But I was in a tough spot because I couldn't afford to waste the food. My friends took their leftovers, so I thought it was okay. Maybe I should have communicated with the host before taking it home, but I didn't know that was necessary. In the end, I think I did what I had to do to manage my resources, but perhaps I should have been more considerate of the host's feelings and the social norms of potlucks. Maybe next time, I should ask if it's okay to take leftovers home before doing so.
